sections.h2: Where do Kalkaska County deeds get recorded?
sections.html:
The Register of Deeds is housed in the Administration Building, 605 N. Birch Street, village of Kalkaska, MI 49646, phone 231-258-3315. Weekday administration hours are 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., and legal holidays are observed. The counter also processes passport applications by appointment only.

Wikipedia places Kalkaska County in northern Lower Michigan, within the Traverse City metropolitan area. Its 571 square miles hold more than 80 lakes and about 275 miles of streams and rivers. Marsh and the Pere Marquette State Forest account for a good deal of the land.

Cabins, lake lots and acreage anywhere in the county all record at this single office. The village of Kalkaska is both the county's only village and its seat.

sections.h2: What will the Kalkaska County office charge to file a deed?
sections.html:
Indexing and recording a deed, mortgage, lis pendens, affidavit or any other instrument takes $30 for the whole paper, with no per page charge since October 1, 2016, the county says. A document discharging or assigning mortgages adds $3 per extra instrument number. See MCL 600.2567.

Warranty covenant deeds, land contracts and land contract assignments need a county treasurer tax certificate first. The county prices it at $5.00 per instrument for as many as five descriptions, then 20 cents for each further description, which matters when a sale spans several parcels.

  • Cards can be used through an online county payment page, with a paycode shown on the register of deeds page.
  • Plat books are sold at the counter for cash or check.
  • A free property fraud alert notifies you of any document recorded with your name in it.

sections.h2: What transfer tax comes out of a Kalkaska County sale?
sections.html:
Any deed worth $100 or more triggers both taxes, and the grantor bears them. The county share is 55 cents per $500 under MCL 207.504, and the state share is $3.75 per $500. The county site carries a chart for looking up any price.

State the property value on the deed, or file a valuation affidavit, which costs nothing but must be noted on the deed. An exemption claimed under MCL 207.505 for the county or MCL 207.526 for the state has to be written on the deed too.

Sample Kalkaska County transfer tax at $4.30 per $500 (county $0.55 plus state $3.75)

The $189,000 row starts from the county's Census median home value of $188,900, rounded up to the next $500 step.

sections.h2: Which Kalkaska County deeds escape the tax?
sections.html:
The two transfer tax acts supply the exemptions, and the county posts both lists on its recording fees page. Both exempt security instruments, leases and deeds given by a government grantor, along with confirmation deeds, for example a quitclaim that fixes a flaw in title the grantee already holds.

Family transfers are treated differently. Only the state act exempts a deed from a parent to a child, stepchild, grandchild or step-grandchild. The same MCL 207.526 also exempts foreclosure deeds and deeds in lieu, though a later resale by the foreclosing party is taxed.

Whichever exemption applies, put it in writing on the deed. If tax was paid on a deed that qualified, the state act lets the seller request a refund from the state treasury.

sections.h2: Does Kalkaska County take electronic filings?
sections.html:
Yes, for all document types except judgments, court orders, plats, surveys and other certified papers. The partner vendors are ePN, CSC, Indecomm and Simplifile, and Simplifile alone handles warranty deeds, land contracts and other treasurer certified papers.

Title professionals sign up for Laredo, the county's records search program, by sending the register of deeds a subscription agreement. Individual owners can use the fraud alert and the front counter.

A one time seller is usually best served when the title company or closing attorney e-records. To carry a paper deed instead, read the layout list below first, because a returned deed can delay closing.

sections.h2: What page layout will the Kalkaska County counter accept?
sections.html:
The state recording statute, MCL 565.201, binds this office like any other, and an instrument missing an item cannot be accepted. Homemade deeds tend to fail on these points:

  • 2.5 inches of open space atop page one, and half inch margins around the rest.
  • Dark print, 10 point type, on white paper no lighter than 20 pound.
  • A single phrase on the first printed line naming what is being recorded.
  • Names printed beneath every signature, and the notary's name beside the notary signature.
  • The grantee's address, plus the drafter's name and business address.
  • An attached English translation when part of the text is in another language.

The statute adds that anything already recorded is conclusively presumed to comply, so a deed that clears the counter stays on record even if a small slip went unnoticed.

sections.h2: How big is the Kalkaska County housing market?
sections.html:
This is a small market where nearly everyone owns. QuickFacts counts 18,693 residents in mid 2025, a gain of 4.2 percent over the April 2020 base, in 11,820 housing units. Owners live in 88.2 percent of occupied homes.

  • Middle home value, 2020 to 2024: $188,900.
  • Rent at the midpoint: $853 a month.
  • Share of residents past 65: 24.6 percent.
  • Mean trip to work: 29.7 minutes, longer than in Jackson or Kalamazoo counties.
  • Density: 32 people per square mile.

Per Wikipedia, US 131 cuts through the western part of the county, M-66 runs north to south in the west center, and M-72 crosses the middle from west to east.

sections.h2: What is the Kalkaska County setting for a house sale?
sections.html:
The area began as Wabassee County in 1840 and took its present name in 1843, according to Wikipedia. It was organized in its own right on January 27, 1871. Kalkaska sand, the Michigan state soil, is named for it, and elevation swings from 595 feet to about 1,246 feet, which makes it one of the more uneven counties in the Lower Peninsula.

Beyond the village of Kalkaska, the communities of Bear Lake, Manistee Lake, Rapid City and South Boardman are census designated places, and the county borders Antrim, Otsego, Crawford, Roscommon, Missaukee, Wexford and Grand Traverse counties. Buyers sometimes arrive from those neighbors, so the closing agent should settle early where each party will sign.

Census figures show 38 building permits in 2025, 4,120 jobs at employer firms in 2023, and 1,384 veterans. Employment slipped 5.9 percent between 2022 and 2023, a point worth knowing when you price a house for a local buyer.

sections.h2: What should I line up before closing on a Kalkaska County sale?
sections.html:
Pick up the certificate and any tax payoff figure from the county treasurer, and let the register of deeds look over your paperwork. Confirm the treasurer's hours and number before you head over, since schedules change.

Agree with your title company on who pays each of these, so nothing is paid twice:

  • The $30 deed filing charge.
  • The treasurer's certificate, $5 for a short parcel list.
  • Both transfer taxes, which land on the seller.

If the sale includes several parcels, count the descriptions early, because each one past five adds 20 cents to the certificate.

faqs.q: What does the Kalkaska County Register of Deeds charge to record a deed?
faqs.a: Thirty dollars covers a whole document of any length. A paper assigning or discharging several mortgages adds $3 for each extra instrument number.

faqs.q: Does a Kalkaska County deed need a tax certificate?
faqs.a: It does when the deed has a warranty covenant, and for land contracts and their assignments. The treasurer charges $5.00 an instrument for up to five descriptions.

faqs.q: Who pays Kalkaska County transfer tax?
faqs.a: The seller does. Recording triggers 55 cents for the county and $3.75 for the state per $500 of price, unless an exemption stated on the deed applies.

faqs.q: Can I pay by card at the Kalkaska County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: Yes. The register of deeds page links a county card payment service and gives a paycode to use. Treat the treasurer's tax certificate fee as a separate payment and ask that office how it takes payment.

faqs.q: What number do I call at the Kalkaska County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: Dial 231-258-3315. The counter is at 605 N. Birch Street in Kalkaska and keeps weekday administration hours.
